{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Licence Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings and proposed redlines

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. The commercial architecture is broadly acceptable to us: there is no exclusivity, non-compete, employee non-solicit, MFN or audit obligation binding Client; there are no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Client; we hold an unrestricted termination-for-convenience right with no exit fee; renewal is annual on a 30-day non-renewal notice; and the minimum monthly fee sits at our fallback because it is term-limited and penalty-free. Governing law and venue (California; San Luis Obispo County courts) sit at our fallback and we do not propose to reopen them.

The risk is concentrated in the protective provisions. Seven items fail the fallback and are redlined: the limitation of liability is one-way against us (Client uncapped, Vendor capped) with no consequential-damages exclusion and no carve-outs; there is no insurance obligation of any kind despite TrueLink hosting our site and processing consumer credit data; TrueLink's indemnity is limited to its own breach, with no IP-infringement, breach-of-law or data-breach cover, while our indemnity is open-ended; the only TrueLink warranty is a Year 2000 warranty; Client has no ownership of or licence to Support Services deliverables and no affirmative retention of its data and IP; the licence does not reach Client affiliates and assignment is blocked without discretionary consent, including on a merger; and there is no transition-assistance or data-return mechanic on exit.

Separately, the minimum monthly fee amounts in § 5(a) are left blank ("not less than $____ per month") and the internal cross-references to "Section 4" appear mis-numbered — commercial and drafting clean-ups to close before signature.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | Licence is expressly non-exclusive and preserves our freedom to source or build alternatives; § 3(i) credit-report tie-in is scoped to Interface-routed transactions only. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No stipulated damages, default interest, late fee or early-termination charge. Minimum-fee blanks to be completed. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No restraint on Client; the referenced Non-Competition Agreement limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data and runs in our favour (not attached — review separately). |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Client may terminate at will with no exit fee; Vendor has no mid-term convenience right. No pro-rata refund language, but fees are billed monthly in arrears. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No vendor audit or usage-verification right; § 6 documentation obligation runs in our favour. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (at fallback) | § 12 INDEMNITY. | California law and California courts; litigation, not arbitration. County-specific venue is Vendor-convenient — raise only if the Agreement is reopened. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No MFN on Client; the MFN and one-year price freeze run in our favour and should be retained. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant (at fallback) | § 5 COMPENSATION. | Minimum monthly fee limited to the current one-year term, with no shortfall charge, take-or-pay or usage cap, and an at-will exit. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No no-hire or non-solicit covenant on Client. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | One-year renewals on a mutual 30-day non-renewal notice. No renewal reminder and no uplift cap — noted only. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only warranty is Year 2000 date handling; no services, conformance, malicious-code or compliance warranty and no remedy. Redline inserts a performance warranty with repair/replace/refund. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Consent-based with an affiliate carve-out only; a merger or asset sale would need TrueLink's discretionary approval. Redline adds successor carve-out, reasonableness standard, competitor bar and no termination on Client change of control. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 12(b) covers TrueLink's own breach only — no IP infringement, breach of law, data breach or wilful misconduct — while § 12(a) is open-ended against us. Redline adds the Vendor indemnity and narrows ours. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance obligation anywhere, though TrueLink hosts the site and processes consumer credit data and its indemnity is unbacked. Redline inserts a new § 31 (CGL, E&O, cyber/privacy, workers' compensation, certificates on request). |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 2 LICENSE. | § 2(d) confirms TrueLink's rights only; nothing gives Client ownership of Support Services work product or confirms retention of Client IP and data. Redline inserts a Client-side § 2(e). |
| Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant runs to Client alone with no affiliate mechanism and no successor exception. Redline adopts the fallback: affiliates on written notice plus M&A successor assignment. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY. | One-way cap protecting TrueLink for §§ 3, 4, 7 and 11 only; Client uncapped, no consequential-damages exclusion, no carve-outs. Redline makes the cap mutual (greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000) and adds Excluded Claims. |
| Low | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** (redline not yet verified) | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No migration assistance, data export, return or deletion obligation; § 13 puts the name-server and re-hosting burden on Client. Proposed insertion after the Termination section has not passed verification and needs manual drafting before it goes out. |

## Walk-away items

These three items are at or approaching the playbook's walk-away thresholds and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trade-ables:

1. **Limitation of liability (§ 12, closing paragraph).** Client's liability is wholly uncapped while TrueLink's is capped and limited to four sections — expressly walk-away territory. We require a mutual cap, an indirect/consequential exclusion and Excluded Claims carve-outs (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with confirmation that Client's payment obligations are not damages.
2. **Vendor insurance (absent).** No coverage obligation of any kind, in a hosting arrangement involving consumer credit data, is walk-away territory under the rule and leaves TrueLink's indemnity unbacked against a 12-month fee cap. We require the new § 31 programme.
3. **Assignment and change of control (§ 15).** Discretionary consent with no successor carve-out means our own merger or sale of substantially all assets is hostage to TrueLink's approval. This approaches walk-away and the successor carve-out is not negotiable.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering WARRANTY, INDEMN, LOL-CAP, INSURANCE, IP, LICENSE and ASSIGN, with a short covering note framing the liability, insurance and assignment items as gating and the balance as conforming clean-ups.
2. **Draft the transition/data-return clause manually.** The automated insertion for TRANSITION did not verify; counsel to draft the exit provision (migration assistance, export in a usable format, return and deletion with certification) for insertion after the Termination section, and confirm it is picked up by the survival language.
3. **Complete the commercial blanks.** Business to confirm the § 5(a) minimum monthly amounts before signature; we will also correct the mis-numbered "Section 4" cross-references and confirm that § 14's "Subject to Section 4" does not extend minimums beyond the notice period.
4. **Obtain the Non-Competition Agreement.** It is cross-referenced at § 8(d) but not attached or defined; we should review it to confirm it imposes no restraint on Client and that the Credit Data protections run in our favour as described.
5. **Note for any reopening (not raised now).** Renewal reminder and a renewal-uplift cap; New York law or a broader California venue; and an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on termination. None of these justifies reopening the Agreement on its own.
"}
